project.title: CD68+ region of rat scar tissue by AutoSTOMP
project.projectDescription: To test the ability of the Automated Spatially Targeted Optical Micro Proteomics (AutoSTOMP) protocol to selectively biotinylate structures of interest within tissue sections we first examined a rat myocardial infarction model. In this model, trauma caused by ligation and infiltrating immune cells causes fibroblast activation and deposition of scar tissue that ultimately impairs cardiac function. Macrophages are thought to play a role in inflammatory regulation and damaged cell turnover in the tissue. We decide to grab the proteome of the macrophage rich regions.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: 8-week-old male Sprague-Dawley rats (Envigo) by left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery permanent ligation.  1-week post-surgery, the scar region was dissected, frozen in liquid-nitrogen-chilled isopentane, and embedded in OTC. 7 μm cryosections were acquired and processed by AutoSTOMP protocol. https://github.com/boris2008/AutoSTOMP_2.0.git. Rat cardiac sections were lysed in the hydroxylamine lysis buffer (1 M NH2OH−HCl, 8 M urea, 0.2 M K2CO3, pH = 9.0) at 45 oC for 17 h to extract proteins. Proteins were precipitated on streptavidin beads. The bound proteins was eluted, processed, and further characterized on Thermo Electron Q Exactive HF-X mass spectrometer.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: The raw mass spectra data were parsed by MaxQuant (versions 1.6.14.0, Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry). The MaxQuant results were then analyzed following the label-free quantification (LFQ) data analysis protocol. Student’s t-test (permutation-based FDR < 0.05) and t-SNE clustering were applied in Perseus (versions 1.6.14.0, Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry). The resulting data were plotted in R (www.r-project.org) with the installed packages “ggplot2”, “ggrepel”, “heatmap.2” or using GraphPad Prism (version 8.2.1).
